R045-01.notes: P2 sets up the irreversibility assumption, P3-P4 give counterexamples, P5 centers children/home, P6 stresses difficulty yet 'outcome is not fixed.' B captures this. A contradicts P5/P6 ('not because of laws or scholarship alone'); C contradicts P6; D contradicts P4.

R045-03.notes: P2 states the 'one-way path to silence' assumption and ends 'Several communities have since challenged that assumption.' B belongs to P4; C is not explained in P2 (it is asserted, not explained); D: no list in P2.

R045-04.notes: D is a reasonable trap (graduates went on to Māori-language primary schools, but those are distinct and not described as bilingual).

R045-05.notes: 'the home as the decisive setting' = the setting that determines whether the language survives. A is the common person-oriented sense (good trap); C 'final' is a weaker trap; D unsupported. Paragraph reference correct (P5).

R045-06.notes: 'A similar approach was adopted in Hawaiʻi' extends the nest model beyond New Zealand. A: no comparison of current speaker counts; B irrelevant; C contradicted ('fewer than fifty children' still spoke it). Fact check: fewer than ~50 child native speakers in early 1980s is consistent with standard accounts (Pūnana Leo from 1983-84). Paragraph reference correct (end of P4).
